summary: This note is an excerpt from a fiction book (Book 4, part 104) narrated by Valentine. It describes how a revolution came about: zombiism drugs were unaffordable, governments failed to negotiate prices, zombies overran the Cabinet, and the crowd killed the PM. The narrative then turns to a day at the cinema with her best friend Leeza, watching movies, buying snacks, and flirting with a boy.
one_line: Valentine recounts the zombie-driven revolution that overthrew the PM, then spends a cinema outing with best friend Leeza.
key_facts: Valentine and her friends have been made to 'Explain the Revolution' as bona fide heroes of the revolution.
The revolution was prompted by a game that Valentine played a lot and thought was quite good, featuring a virtual city modeled on her own city.
Three governments promised to negotiate better prices for zombiism drugs and all three failed.
The Cabinet was overrun by zombies who tore three MPs to bits and infected seven more.
The crowd carried the PM out of her office, put her in a barrel, drove nails through it, and rolled it into the river.
The new PM refused to negotiate drug prices and instead built zombiism drug factories in the city, giving the drug away in spray, pill and needle form.
Under the new government, copies of movies, songs, drugs, buildings and cars were made right there in the city.
Valentine and Leeza, her best friend that week, watched a movie together with their arms around each other's shoulders.
The movie was about a woman in love with two men who hated each other, and the audio was dubbed over from English.
The cinema was celebrating its opening day with chocolates, brown beer for adults, and fizzy elderflower for kids.
Valentine tripped a cute boy whom Leeza liked, so he nearly fell into Leeza's lap.
The next picture barely had time to start before it was shut off.
